fields.Front: In the 'nuts and bolts' view, what are the four kinds of physical components that make up the Internet?
fields.Back:
1) Hosts = end systems: billions of devices at the edge running network apps; clients and servers (servers mostly in data centers).
2) Packet switches: routers (core) and link-layer switches (access nets) forward packets (chunks of data).
3) Communication links: fiber, copper, coax, radio, satellite; transmission rate = bandwidth = capacity, in bps.
4) Networks: devices + routers + links managed by one organization (home, enterprise, mobile, datacenter, content provider, ISP).

fields.Front: Describe the 'service view' of the Internet: what two things does it provide to applications?
fields.Back:
1) An infrastructure that provides services to distributed applications: Web, streaming video, teleconferencing, email, games, e-commerce, social media, connected appliances.
2) A programming interface: 'hooks' (the socket API) let sending/receiving apps connect to and use the Internet transport service, with a choice of service options, analogous to a postal service offering ordinary vs registered mail (later: UDP vs TCP).

fields.Front: Which body develops Internet standards, what are the documents called, what do they define, and which body handles Ethernet/WiFi?
fields.Back:
IETF (Internet Engineering Task Force) publishes RFCs (Requests for Comments), which define TCP, IP, HTTP, SMTP and thousands of other protocols so vendors interoperate.
Link-level standards such as Ethernet and WiFi (802.x) come from the IEEE 802 committee.

fields.Text: Hosts are also called {{c1::end systems}}; they run network applications at the Internet's {{c1::edge}}. Informally they are {{c1::clients}} (request) or {{c1::servers}} (store/serve content, usually in data centers).
Packet switches forward packets from an incoming link to an outgoing link; the two main kinds are {{c1::routers}} (network core) and {{c1::link-layer switches}} (access networks).
fields.Extra: Routers implement 3 layers of the stack; switches implement 2.

fields.Text: The Internet is a '{{c1::network of networks}}' made of interconnected {{c1::ISPs}} and {{c1::nobody owns it}}; you reach it through an {{c1::access ISP}}, which connects to larger ISPs. Internet standards come from the {{c1::IETF}} as {{c1::RFCs}}.
